theory.title: Passive forms with modal verbs
theory.explanation: Use modal + be + past participle to describe rules, possibilities and requirements when the action is more important than the person doing it. For past possibility or criticism, use modal + have been + past participle.
theory.tip: Observa si hablas de una experiencia terminada, una posibilidad, una habilidad o una norma. Esa diferencia determina la estructura.

content.passage: The workshop has introduced new safety rules. Protective glasses must be worn when machines are being used, and all tools should be checked before work begins. Damaged equipment must not be used. Any problems have to be reported to the supervisor immediately. Visitors may be asked to wait outside during repairs. The new instructions can be found beside the entrance, and they should be read by everyone before starting a task. These simple steps can prevent serious accidents.

content.audioTranscript: A: The centre has a new training programme. B: Who can join? A: Adult students who want to improve their skills. B: How do they apply for the course? A: They send their applications online. B: When will they receive confirmation? A: Within five working days. B: Who can they contact if they need help? A: The office.
